summary: Project financial management and cost recovery training with Excel, EVM, and practical budgeting tools. Build control, recovery, and reporting skills.
lede: Project financial management and cost recovery covers how to plan, track and report project costs against budgets and funding conditions. It is designed for finance and project professionals handling budgets, invoices or reporting who need to control spending and determine which costs can be recovered. Learners practise setting cost baselines, analyzing burn rates and variances, calculating indirect cost recovery, and preparing financial reports, with operational introductions to Earned Value Management and Power BI.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for finance and project professionals who already handle budgets, invoices, or reporting and need stronger control over project costs and recovery. It also suits adjacent roles that influence chargeability, approvals, and funding compliance.
prerequisites: You should bring a laptop with Microsoft Excel installed and be ready to work with sample project cost data, budget templates, and reporting formats. A calculator and familiarity with basic project finance terminology will help you complete the exercises efficiently. If your organization uses a specific chart of accounts, budget code structure, or donor reporting template, you may also bring a sanitized example for adaptation during the workshop.
